title: Universal curve-test datum for a failure
statement:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

with both squares Cartesian, where

1. $S'$ is affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed
function field;
1. $K$ is algebraically closed and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is
dominant (in other words $K$ is an extension of the function
field of $S'$),

and there exists an integer $d\mid n$ such that
$R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)$ is nonzero.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.7, [Tag `0F08`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F08).*)

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-bc-failure-field] to obtain an affine $S_0$, a base change $f_0:X_0\to S_0$, a field $K_0$, $g_0:\operatorname{Spec}K_0\to S_0$, and an $n$-annihilated sheaf $F_0$ whose degree-$q$ base-change arrow is not an isomorphism. The cumulative universal hypothesis includes every degree required by that lemma. Both schemes at the ends of $g_0$ are affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) gives that $g_0$ is qcqs.

Pass to K = AlgebraicClosure K0. The induced spectrum map is integral because the extension is algebraic, and is surjective because both spectra have one point. Universality gives degree q-1 base change for f0. Apply [lem-sbc-module-bc-integral-surjective] to the pasted field square: an isomorphism after this test-base replacement would imply the original isomorphism, contradicting failure.

Apply [lem-sbc-normalization-algclosed-field] to the geometric point of the affine base. Obtain the affine integral normal S-double-prime, integral pi, algebraically closed function field, and geometric generic-point lift g-double-prime. Form the two pullback squares and paste the base-change square with the original one. If the inner degree-q module base-change arrow were invertible, [lem-sbc-module-integral-base-change-iso] would make the pasted arrow invertible, contradicting the surviving failure. Thus failure survives normalization without first changing coefficient categories.

The cumulative universal hypothesis gives degree q-1 base change on the twice-base-changed morphism by pasting the Cartesian squares. Apply the fixed-base injectivity lemma [lem-sbc-fixed-base-critical-map]. A monomorphism into a zero target has zero source and is therefore an isomorphism, contradicting failure. The target is nonzero. The fibre projection h is affine, hence qcqs, as the base change of the map g-double-prime between affine schemes.

The field-failure coefficient is already a module sheaf over Lambda = ULift(ZMod n), and n vanishes in Lambda. Apply [lem-sbc-prime-cyclic-detection] directly to the nonzero base-change target, the algebraically closed field, and the qcqs map h. It yields a prime r dividing n with nonzero higher direct image of the constant module P/(r), where P = ULift(ZMod r). No intermediate scalar-restriction comparison is needed at this step.

In P = ULift(ZMod r), r = 0, so (r) is the bottom ideal and Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot identifies P/(r) with P. Forget this linear isomorphism to an additive one. The module forgetful functor is a left adjoint (restriction from integers followed by the equivalence between integer modules and abelian groups), so constantCommuteCompose identifies the underlying constant sheaf. Apply [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison], then map the constant-sheaf isomorphism through abelian higher direct image. A zero abelian result would make the forgotten module higher direct image zero. Faithfulness reflects zero objects by the identity-equals-zero criterion, contradicting the prime witness. Take d = r and equip each pullback square with its canonical isoPullback, whose two projection equations give ChosenCartesianSquare.

lean.note: Uses the recorded cumulative universal predicate at q-1 and its fixed-degree universal predicate with ULift (ZMod n). The conclusion is abelian higher direct image of the actual constant cyclic group ULift (ZMod d), not the arbitrary-coefficient quotient in the upstream theorem. ChosenCartesianSquare gives both Cartesian identifications. Stalk integral closedness together with IsIntegral expresses normality; i induces the dominant geometric generic point.

blueprint_update.statement:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \longleftarrow & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow h\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

with both squares Cartesian, where

1. $S'$ is affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed
function field;
1. $K$ is algebraically closed and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is
dominant (in other words $K$ is an extension of the function
field of $S'$),

and there exists an integer $d\mid n$ such that
$R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)$ is nonzero.

proof.text:
By [sbc-lem-bc-failure-field] there are a morphism $S'\to S$ with
$S'$ affine, the base change $f':X'\to S'$, a field $K$ with a morphism
$T=\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$, and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T$
annihilated by $n$ for which the degree-$q$ base-change map of $f'$
along $T\to S'$ is not an isomorphism. By
[sbc-lem-bc-integral-surjective] (whose hypothesis, $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q-1)$
universally, is part of ours) applied to
the base change $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}K$
to an algebraic closure $K'$ of $K$ (an integral surjective morphism),
we may assume $K$ is algebraically closed. A sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules on a geometric point is a direct sum of
copies of $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ for varying $d\mid n$, so by the
finite direct-sum and retract case of the map, we may assume
$\mathcal F$ is constant with value $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ for some
$d\mid n$ (the cokernel of the base-change map
$\bigl(R^qh_*(c)\bigr)$ decomposes accordingly). Finally, by
[sbc-lem-bc-integral-base] applied to
$\pi:S''\to S'$ the normalization of $S'$ in
$\operatorname{Spec}K$ (integral: the integral closure of the normal
domain $A'$ in $K$ is integral over $A'$, commutative algebra),
with $X''=X'\times_{S'}S''$, we may replace $S'$ by $S''$, which is
affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed function field
$K$; this is the datum of the statement.
